home.title:
Making community plugins
look like one product.
home.lede: DeepSeek Harness gives plugin authors a technical stack and a development contract, but no design spec: how large a control should be, how much space belongs between two of them, how long a transition runs, how to draw an icon, or who wins when two plugins want the same spot. This resource supplies that layer — every number carries its source, and every component is ready to use.
home.sectionHint: Collected by scripts from a running harness; everything is reproducible

why.title: Why
why.body: The product shipped compatibility for the stack but not for design — that is why this repository exists.

why.title: Why this spec exists
why.lede: In one line: the product gave plugins a stack that runs, not a spec that looks consistent.
why.scopeTitle: What this repository will not do

items.tokens: A complete semantic token set: colour, elevation and state all have official values.
items.primitives: Shared control primitives (button, pill, tag, switch, input, menu, modal, toast…), with an explicit instruction not to copy a control that already exists.
items.seats: A seat system where every seat declares its purpose, registration contract and shadowing risk.
items.icons: An icon set with a consistent naming scheme and size families.
items.layout: No layout spec: which region a plugin may occupy, how much of it, and how it coordinates with the conversation area are all unstated.
items.order: No placement contract: on a list seat, the order value is left to good intentions.
items.motion: No motion spec: durations and curves are not unified.
items.iconGeometry: No icon geometry: stroke weight and optical alignment for a self-drawn glyph have no reference.
items.conflict: No arbitration: when two plugins want the same seat or the same visual space, nothing tells anyone.
items.aesthetics: It does not judge aesthetics. The spec keeps things consistent and usable; it does not claim one style is prettier.
items.force: It does not force anyone to change their code. A spec is a shared reference for those who opt in.
items.invent: It does not invent numbers. Every size, gap and duration carries its source, and where no authority exists it says so.

why.closing: This is not one plugin's fault; it is what happens without a spec and a check. This resource does two things: fills the gap, and makes conflicts visible.

spec.title: Design spec
spec.lede: In reading order. If this ecosystem is new to you, start with the frame layout and seat selection.

components.title: Reusable source
components.lede: Every component is a dependency-free React implementation that uses official tokens only, and carries its geometry source and when-to-use. Copy and go.
components.docSpecNote: This one is for agents and engineers: geometry sources, API, tokens and machine-checkable constraints.
components.chineseOnly: This component's documentation is currently Chinese-only.
components.usage: The component directory is an npm package and can be installed; a single folder can also be copied straight into your plugin.

seats.title: Seat directory
seats.lede: The harness declares {n} UI seats. Your plugin can only live in one of them — choosing the wrong seat costs more than writing the wrong style.
seats.riskyNote: {n} seats carry a shadowing risk of shadows-shipped-ui: occupying one replaces official UI. Use those only when you really mean to replace it.

kinds.single: single — one occupant; a later registration shadows an earlier one
kinds.list: list — several plugins, ordered ascending by order
kinds.chain: chain — selector-routed, may replace the whole chain

scopes.root: root — global, exists without a session
scopes.session: session — renders only with a selected session

seats.orderNote: Start with the list seat whose meaning fits best; fall back to a single seat only when nothing fits; treat seats with replaceRisk shadows-shipped-ui as a last resort.

icons.title: Official icon set
icons.lede: {n} icons, all extracted from the product's own client bundle, with path data untouched. Naming: ic_ds_<name>_<style>_<size>. Click any icon to copy its SVG.
icons.familyTail: A self-drawn glyph should match the visual weight and stroke weight of the icons beside it.
icons.why: Mismatched icon style is where a plugin interface gives itself away. The official set already has its visual weight and padding worked out; reusing it is less work than drawing something "close enough", and it is consistent.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.lede: {palette} raw palette values back {aliases} semantic aliases. A plugin should use the aliases only — light and dark are the product's job.
tokens.usageNote: Usage: color: var(--dsw-alias-label-primary). A hard-coded colour is the number one reason plugins break in dark mode.
tokens.depth: Express depth with background layers (bg-base → bg-layer-1 → bg-layer-2 → bg-overlay), not with shadows. A shadow is the exception, not the default.
tokens.source: Values come straight from the theme definition inside the product's client bundle, one set per theme, unmodified.

lab.motionNote: Pick a duration and a curve, then play: the block runs once. A duration in a spec should not be a number on paper — 350ms against 100ms is clearer in one glance than in ten lines of prose.
